extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: C-EVAL is the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13948 multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, and professional) spanning 52 diverse disciplines ranging from humanities to science and engineering. It is accompanied by C-EVAL HARD, a subset of very challenging subjects requiring advanced reasoning abilities.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2023 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from mock exams and small-scale local exams freely available on the internet, as well as past exam questions from top universities in China shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website. Data came primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams and small-scale local exams available online (primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents), past exam questions from top universities in China, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents are initially processed into text. All questions are subsequently parsed – automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors – into a structured format. For subjects with complex mathematical notations, they are manually converted into standard LaTeX formats. All questions are processed to include exactly four choices; questions with fewer than four options are eliminated and incorrect choices are randomly dropped for questions with more than four options. All questions go through standard data preprocessing pipeline including deduplication and cleaning. Questions undergo several rounds of human validation by the authors, and all LaTeX notations are ensured to be compiled without syntax errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were parsed and annotated by the authors into a structured format. For the development split, explanations were generated by first prompting GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanations for the ground-truth answer, then manually revised by the authors to obtain the final explanations.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Ground-truth labels of the development and validation splits are released, while labels of the test split are kept private. Users submit model predictions to https://cevalbenchmark.com to obtain test accuracy, where a public leaderboard is maintained.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: English benchmarks tend to exhibit geographical biases towards the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them, which motivated the creation of C-EVAL for Chinese context.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL, along with all English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness. Data contamination risk exists as exam questions from national tests may be crawled into LLM pretraining data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation and benchmarking of large language models (LLMs) in a Chinese context, assessing advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities. Can be used in zero-shot and few-shot settings, as well as chain-of-thought evaluation. The validation set is intended for hyperparameter tuning.
